attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts what the pricing website displayed.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the website-display claim and both device presentations.

contract.note: Reading mobile and desktop as website presentations is ordinary in context. Requiring evidence for both preserves the stated scope.

evidence.note: Timely reporting establishes the general pricing-page episode but does not distinguish mobile and desktop displays.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes a temporary pricing-page change but supplies neither independent verification of both presentations nor contemporaneous evidence disproving either presentation.

attribution.note: The statement is Zitron's own account of the pricing-page changes.

semantics.note: The central proposition and multiple-page scope are preserved, but the normalisation omits the source's late-afternoon timing qualifier.

contract.note: The surrounding text supports advertised benefits as the subject. Requiring multiple pricing pages fairly preserves the plural scope; the unspecified timezone limits timing precision.

evidence.note: Reporting cites a separate observer of Pro exclusion on the pricing page. It supports the central observation but does not establish multiple affected pages or the precise start time.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports removal from the main pricing page during the episode. It does not establish the asserted multiple-page scope or late-afternoon timing. Missing corroboration does not establish contradiction.

attribution.note: Zitron endorses the documentation claim and the criticism; the experiment percentage is attributed to Anthropic.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the factual uniformity assertion and accompanying criticism. The factual component is assessable separately from the evaluative language.

contract.note: Assessing public messaging and its asserted uniformity is fair. Confusing documentation does not itself establish that the reported experiment percentage was false.

evidence.note: Anthropic acknowledges documentation changes confusing people outside the experiment. This is a company disclosure supporting the messaging criticism, not independent verification of enrollment.
The reporter observed the product page still advertising Pro access during the episode, contradicting uniform website exclusion.

reviews.rationale: Broadly visible exclusion messaging and the resulting confusion are supported. Uniform exclusion across relevant pages is contradicted by the contemporaneous product-page observation. The actual experiment percentage remains independently unverified.

attribution.note: Zitron expresses his own expectation that comparable changes will recur.

semantics.note: The proposition fairly captures an unqualified expectation of recurrence. The metadata's probability label is unwarranted: expressing a belief does not automatically make an otherwise firm expectation probabilistic.

contract.note: Comparable subscription restrictions introduced with little notice are an ordinary contextual reading of the manner described. The contract appropriately supplies no deadline.

evidence.note: The company disclosure says the proposed restriction was paused and subscription usage continued. It does not establish an implemented recurrence.
The report describes a scheduled reduction with advance notice. It does not establish an implemented restriction introduced in the comparable manner required by the contract.

reviews.rationale: The statement expresses an unqualified expectation of recurrence without a deadline. Neither candidate establishes the contract's conclusive event. The elapsed interval without a verified comparable event cannot contradict this open-ended forecast.
